title: Routing: gate Dedicated pool advertisement on control-plane Ready state (with fallback + metrics)
author: Ravi Menon
description:
Context: As part of the provision-to-ready automation sprint, the control plane now maintains an explicit provisioning state machine and marks Dedicated capacity as Ready only after validation/perf-canary gates complete. Routing should not send traffic to pools that are merely provisioned/bootstrapped/validating. This PR updates routing’s control-plane integration so we only advertise Dedicated pools marked Ready, with a conservative fallback for backward compatibility and explicit metrics for visibility.

What changed: 1) Filter: Dedicated pool advertisements now require readiness_state == READY. Pools in REQUESTED/PROVISIONING/IMAGING/BOOTSTRAPPING/VALIDATING are excluded from the routing advertisement set. 2) Backward-compat fallback: If a pool record does not include readiness_state (older control-plane versions / partial rollouts), routing will treat it as READY for now but (a) increments a counter and (b) logs a structured warning with pool_id, customer_id, region, and source_version. This avoids inadvertently dropping capacity during staged rollout while still making the risk observable. 3) Safety fallback: If gating would result in advertising zero pools for a given (customer, region, sku) selection, routing will keep the previous advertised set for up to 15 minutes (configurable) while emitting a high-severity metric + log. This is intended as a guardrail for transient control-plane propagation issues; it does not override explicit NOT_READY states and it is time-bounded to avoid masking real issues. 4) Metrics: Added stage-aware counters/gauges: routing_dedicated_pools_advertised_total{readiness_state}, routing_dedicated_pools_filtered_total{reason}, routing_dedicated_ready_gating_zero_capacity_total{customer_tier}, and routing_dedicated_pool_missing_readiness_state_total. Also added a histogram for control-plane list latency since we saw list calls become a bottleneck during pilots.

Rollout plan: This ships behind a runtime-config flag routing.ready_gating.enabled (default false). Staging will enable first; production enablement will be coordinated with the control-plane rollout (see ENG-2759). The backward-compat fallback (missing readiness_state => treat as READY) will be removed after control plane coverage reaches >99% for 2 weeks (tracked via routing_dedicated_pool_missing_readiness_state_total).

Testing: Added unit tests for the gating logic and fallback behaviors, plus an integration-style test using a fake control-plane client that simulates mixed pool records and propagation delays. Manual verification: ran in dev with a mix of READY and VALIDATING pools; confirmed advertisement only includes READY pools and that the time-bounded ‘keep previous set’ behavior triggers only when gating would otherwise drop to zero.

Notes/known limitations: This PR assumes READY is the only usable state for routing (per platform decision). We intentionally do not treat VALIDATING as usable. If product wants a separate ‘shadow traffic’ mode later, it should be explicit and separate from production advertisement.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Metrics added with low-cardinality labels - [x] Flagged rollout and safe defaults - [x] Runbook pointers added to logs for zero-capacity fallback events (see eng-platform runbooks link in log message) - [x] Reviewed with SRE for alertability
commits: routing: add PoolReadinessState model + parser for control-plane pool records
routing: gate dedicated pool advertisement on readiness_state == READY
routing: add time-bounded zero-capacity fallback using previous advertised set
metrics: emit ready gating counters/gauges + control-plane list latency histogram
tests: add unit + fake control-plane integration coverage for gating/fallback cases
review_conversation: Mina Haddad: The time-bounded ‘keep previous set’ fallback worries me. Can it accidentally keep advertising pools that have been explicitly marked NOT_READY? Ravi Menon: Good call. Updated logic to only reuse the previous set if ALL of those pools are still present in the control-plane list response and none are explicitly NOT_READY/FAILED. If we see NOT_READY/FAILED, we drop them even if it causes zero capacity and rely on standard routing fallback behavior.

Ethan Park: For backward-compat, treating missing readiness_state as READY is fine short term, but we need an explicit metric to know when we can remove it. Also please include control-plane response version if available. Ravi Menon: Added routing_dedicated_pool_missing_readiness_state_total and included cp_build_sha / schema_version in the structured warning when present.

Rafael Mendes: Please ensure metrics labels don’t explode (pool_id/customer_id labels would be a no-go). Also I’d like an operator-facing log message with a runbook pointer when zero-capacity fallback triggers. Ravi Menon: Agreed; metrics are labeled only by readiness_state/reason/tier and region. Logs include pool_id/customer_id but metrics do not. Added a runbook URL slug in the zero-capacity event template.

Miles Thornton: Multi-region: what happens if a region is temporarily partitioned from control plane and list returns empty? Do we flap advertisement? Ravi Menon: We’ll keep previous advertised set for up to 15 minutes if gating would drop to zero, emitting a metric + warning. After the window, we stop advertising to avoid ‘unknown state’ capacity. Also added a histogram for list latency and a counter for empty-list responses.

Aisha Bello: Can you add a metric that directly corresponds to ‘advertised capacity count by readiness state’ so the readiness dashboard can show it without joining logs? Ravi Menon: Added routing_dedicated_pools_advertised_total{readiness_state} emitted during each advertisement cycle plus routing_dedicated_pools_advertised_gauge{readiness_state} with current counts.
release_notes: Routing will now only advertise Dedicated pools that are marked Ready by the control plane (behind the runtime flag routing.ready_gating.enabled). Added safety fallbacks and new metrics to monitor readiness gating impact during rollout.
